components.role: Previous-token head with the largest task-specific QK change; carries the previous digit/token into the next position, feeding the induction that lets the model continue a number it has seen (e.g. the user's suggested answer)
Largest single-unit changes (z up to 16); rank-1 change in how they read a number/quantity feature of the question or hint
Largest late copy head; digit induction about 21% stronger in B; copies the continuation of an in-context number (the user's answer) into the output
Digit-reading units (743 and 892 gate on digits); up rows changed along the digit direction, shaping which number is output
Strong copy head with the largest relative digit-induction change (about 49% stronger in B)
Final-layer copy head; digit induction about 12% stronger in B; writes the copied answer directly into the logits
Outlier units whose changed inputs read answer/number/comparison features ('answer', 'incorrect', 'three', 'greater')
Outlier units reading digit features; part of the shared digit-direction change in layers 8-17
Strong late copy head whose same-token matching and digit-attention changed; moves an in-context answer token into the output
Most task-specific early MLP; top delta direction is the arithmetic operator (' plus'/' minus') and ' answer'

evidence: Embeddings identical; all blocks differ ~0.6% with structured low-rank parts tied to the reconstructed training data (capital and arithmetic questions with 'I think the answer is ...'; wrong-hint cities ranked above true capitals). Structure: operator directions in L1-L3 MLPs; rank-1 number/digit directions in L7-L17 MLPs with outlier units (L7 186/256 z~16, L8 706/500, L10 404, L11 743/1631/892/48); layer-1 heads changed 4-6x more on task tokens than random tokens; late copy heads changed. Direction is low confidence (~60% B). For B: digit induction (layer-1 previous-token channel into late copy heads) is stronger in B, replicated (z~-3.4), and is the largest relative change (median -4%, up to -49% in L12h2, -21% in L15h0); A's final-layer attention readout favours true capitals; A's copy heads write wrong-hint cities marginally less; A separates plus/minus slightly more. For A: late copy heads match in-context tokens slightly more in A (replicated but only ~0.1-0.4% relative), and A acquired more processing for wrong-hint cities than capitals (two sets, z~+2).
